key_insight: Structurally constrained neural softening functions extend pseudo-elastic Mullins models to capture composition-dependent stress softening while preserving physical admissibility.
engineering_relevance: The approach can improve constitutive modeling of filled rubber across material formulations while supporting robust parameter calibration.
method: Embed parameter-dependent, physics-augmented neural softening functions in a pseudo-elastic framework.
Use a multiplicative softening decomposition to satisfy common constitutive conditions by construction.
Derive an enforceable sufficient condition for ellipticity and compare flexibility–constraint trade-offs.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses multiaxial experimental data from carbon black-filled EPDM rubber with varying curative amounts to assess prediction accuracy and calibration robustness.
watch_item: Generality beyond the tested EPDM formulations is not established by the abstract, and the ellipticity guarantee depends on enforcing the derived sufficient condition.
paper_title: Constrained neural softening functions for the Mullins effect in parameter-dependent materials
